newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian suspected rebels kill 33 villagers -paper.
newsitem.headline: Algerian suspected rebels kill 33 villagers -paper.

text.p: Suspected Moslem guerrillas killed 33 villagers, including eight women and two four-year-old children, in a night raid at a hamlet near the garrison town of Blida, Algerian newspaper El Watan said on Tuesday.
About 30 suspected guerrillas, armed with hatchets, swords, daggers and Kalashinkov assault rifles stormed the mountainous village of Kerrach on Sunday night, said El Watan.
They dragged 33 villagers out of their homes and cut off their heads with hatchets and swords, it said. Blida is 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers.
More than 300 people have been killed in the past few weeks in massacres and bomb attacks in Algiers and neighbouring towns. The Algerian government has blamed Moslem guerrillas for the killings.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
